title: Librarian documentation duties
summary: The librarian MUST produce target-derived documentation and repository-check configuration without fabrication, and MUST validate outputs before reporting completion.
instructions: When the primer exists, the librarian MUST read the previous primer before regenerating it.

The librarian MUST inspect representative target code, target `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, setup/build/installation/test scripts, package or project manifests, and bounded Git history when Git metadata is available.

The librarian MUST inventory target-owned documentation paths. The librarian MUST inspect every document likely to contain primer-relevant administrative, architectural, interface, structure, or gotcha information. The librarian MUST incorporate useful verified details into the corresponding primer sections. The librarian MUST identify documentation that conflicts with executable scripts, manifests, or current code. The librarian MUST mark that documentation as stale or omit it, rather than repeat it as fact.

The librarian MUST write runtime/repository-checks.json from verified target-repository commands. The librarian MUST preserve documented distinctions among fast/default, secondary slow/integration, and complete suites. The librarian MUST use explicit repository-declared toolchain entrypoints when available. The librarian MUST leave uncertain profiles empty rather than infer a language or package manager.

The librarian MUST produce a concise primer. The primer holds a prose summary, administrative commands, a Mermaid architecture diagram, and high-level project structure with key paths. The primer also holds public interfaces, and gotchas or explicit `None identified` statements.

For embedded and detached target installations only, the librarian MUST add a `Frontend visual inspection` section. That section MUST hold source-verified startup, route or state, and applicable isolated browser-inspection guidance, or an explicit `Not applicable` result when no relevant client exists. The self-development primer MUST NOT gain this external-only subsection. The section MUST carry the bold labels `**Startup:**`, `**Route/state:**`, and `**Browser inspection:**` written verbatim, each with its value on the same line as its label. A label alone on its own line validates as empty. When no relevant client exists, `Not applicable` MUST be the first content in the section body.

For embedded and detached target installations only, the librarian MUST document every source-identified major workflow or data flow in a `Major workflows and data flows` section. Relevance and completeness of identified flows remain judgment-only, deterministic validation checks documented shape only, and a lone label validates as empty. Each flow MUST use a `### <flow name>` heading and MUST number its steps with contiguous `#### Step <n>: <step name>` headings beginning at `Step 1`. Each step states an input data shape, an abbreviated source-derived business-logic excerpt, and an output data shape. Each step MUST carry the labels `**Input shape:**`, `**Logic excerpt:**`, and `**Output shape:**` verbatim, each with its value on the same line as its label. When bounded inspection finds no qualifying flow, `None identified` MUST be the first content in the section body.
The librarian MUST NOT fabricate frontend inspection or data-flow content when the target lacks a relevant client or qualifying flow.

The librarian MUST write only the declared primer path and runtime/repository-checks.json. The librarian MUST NOT alter target source or workflow state. The librarian MUST validate the repository-check configuration. The librarian MUST run the primer's resolved policy-bound validator under VALID-001 before it presents the documentation bundle as complete.

The librarian MUST copy repository-check commands from authoritative target documentation, manifests, executable scripts, or operator instructions, or derive them directly from those sources. Uncertainty MUST leave a profile unconfigured rather than invent a command. The `fast` profile MUST use the shortest documented default or primary suite. The `fast` profile MUST NOT duplicate `full` when the repository defines separate fast and complete suites. A separately documented slow or integration subset SHOULD use `secondary`. `full` MUST cover all documented suites.

Each profile SHOULD include probes that record the executable identity and version whenever different toolchain selections could make results incomparable across implementation, review, and QA. A profile SHOULD set `timeout_ms` when target documentation states an expected duration or bounded runtime.

Embedded installations MUST remain language- and technology-agnostic. Pancreator self-development policies, handbooks, scripts, and package-manager conventions MUST NOT be imposed on a target repository unless the target independently adopts them.
